documents.text:
Lost company laptop

A staff member who loses a company laptop must contact the service desk immediately and provide the asset tag if known. The service desk marks the device as missing and starts a remote lock request.
documents.title: Lost company laptop

documents.text:
Account protection after device loss

After a lost company laptop report, the security team revokes the affected login sessions. The employee changes the account password after security confirms that session revocation is complete.
documents.title: Account protection after device loss

documents.text:
Equipment for a new employee

A new employee requests a laptop through the equipment form five working days before the first day. The support team prepares the machine and leaves it at the service desk for collection.
documents.title: Equipment for a new employee

documents.text:
First account activation

Before a new employee can use the work account, the line manager sends an activation code. The employee must enroll a second authentication factor before opening internal applications.
documents.title: First account activation

documents.text:
Travel expense submission

Travel expense packets must be submitted within seven calendar days after returning from a business trip. Include the itinerary and available receipts in the expense portal.
documents.title: Travel expense submission

documents.text:
Missing taxi receipts

A taxi expense normally needs a receipt showing the date, amount and journey. If the receipt is lost, attach a signed missing-receipt statement and obtain the manager's approval.
documents.title: Missing taxi receipts

documents.text:
Unexpected search service outage

For an unexpected search service outage, page the on-call engineer through the incident channel. The engineer opens an incident log and assigns a technical responder.
documents.title: Unexpected search service outage

documents.text:
Public outage updates

During an unexpected search service outage, the communications owner posts a status-page update every twenty minutes. A final update must say when service was restored and summarize the customer impact.
documents.title: Public outage updates

documents.text:
Nightly snapshot retention

The archive job creates a snapshot every night. Nightly snapshots are retained for fourteen days in the backup store before the rotation job removes the oldest copy.
documents.title: Nightly snapshot retention

documents.text:
Checking backup recovery

On the first Friday of each month, the recovery team restores a recent snapshot into an isolated test environment. They compare record counts with the saved manifest and record whether the recovery check passed.
documents.title: Checking backup recovery

documents.text:
Gradual feature release

A new feature starts behind a feature flag for five percent of users. The release captain may increase exposure to twenty-five percent after one hour if the error and latency checks remain within the release limits.
documents.title: Gradual feature release

documents.text:
Reverting a feature flag

The release captain has authority to disable a feature flag immediately when the release checks fail. Disabling the flag returns users to the previous behavior without waiting for a new software deployment.
documents.title: Reverting a feature flag

documents.text:
Workspace erasure timeline

A workspace owner can request erasure after ownership is verified. The service team removes the active workspace and its message content within three working days of that verification.
documents.title: Workspace erasure timeline

documents.text:
Billing fields outside workspace erasure

Invoice numbers and tax totals are kept in a separate billing ledger and are outside the workspace erasure operation. Workspace message bodies are not billing records and must not be copied into that ledger.
documents.title: Billing fields outside workspace erasure

documents.text:
Meeting room reservations

Book meeting rooms in Room Board before use. A reservation can last at most two hours, and an unused room reservation should be cancelled after ten minutes.
documents.title: Meeting room reservations

documents.text:
Quiet pod reservations

Quiet pods are single-person spaces for private calls. Reserve a pod in Room Board, and keep each reservation to no more than thirty minutes.
documents.title: Quiet pod reservations

documents.text:
Visitor registration before arrival

A visitor's host registers the guest's name and arrival time in the reception portal at least one working day before the visit. Reception uses this entry to prepare the arrival check.
documents.title: Visitor registration before arrival

documents.text:
Visitor badges and escort

Reception gives an approved visitor a temporary badge after checking identity. A host must escort the visitor in restricted areas, and the badge must be returned to reception before departure.
documents.title: Visitor badges and escort

documents.text:
Joining a training course

Choose a training course from the learning catalog and obtain the line manager's approval before enrolling. The learning coordinator confirms the seat and sends the course joining instructions.
documents.title: Joining a training course

documents.text:
Recording paid learning time

Staff may record up to four paid learning hours each month. Enter those hours under the LEARN project code in the weekly timesheet and attach the course completion confirmation.
documents.title: Recording paid learning time

documents.text:
Beacon travel expense deadline

In the Beacon workspace, a travel expense packet is due within twenty-three calendar days after returning. This deadline belongs only to Beacon and must not replace another workspace's expense policy.
documents.title: Beacon travel expense deadline

documents.text:
Beacon visitor access

Beacon visitors receive an orange temporary badge at reception. The host escorts the visitor in marked access zones and returns the orange badge when the visitor leaves.
documents.title: Beacon visitor access
